title: The Bull and the Ass
logline: A kind-hearted donkey teaches an overworked bull to play sick, the merchant who understands animals sends the donkey to plough instead, and the donkey has to scare the bull back to work with a lie.
moral: Clever advice can land on the adviser; you only know another's work when you have carried it for a day.
tone: Warm farmyard comedy of role reversal: lazy comfort, a sly plan, instant comeuppance, a second sly plan. Gentle, never cruel; the humour comes from faces, mirrored staging and the audience knowing more than the animals.

beats.summary: A merchant's farm with a bull and a donkey.
The bull ploughs under the sun every day and comes home worn out.
The donkey eats well and sleeps most of the time.
The bull's complaint: you are lucky.
The donkey's plan: pretend to be ill, lie down, refuse food.
Planted irony: the merchant listens at the window.
The bull plays sick and the worker cannot move him.
The merchant understands animal speech and heard the plan.
Take the donkey instead: the adviser pays for his advice.
The donkey ploughs for hours and returns broken.
The rested bull thanks him warmly; the donkey seethes at himself.
The donkey's lie: stay ill and you go to the butcher.
The bull trembles; the donkey hides a smirk.
Next morning the bull leaps up, eats everything and goes to plough.
The donkey recovers, having tasted a day of his friend's work.

scenes.summary: The donkey stays in the stable getting his breath back, having tasted one day of his friend's work. Through the window the bull ploughs in the distance. THE END.

camera.notes: CAM on the donkey {x:680,y:740,zoom:1.7}; from 172.4 slow pull-out to {x:560,y:690,zoom:1.2} so the window with the far bull sits above him; hold from 176.0.

scenes.composition: Donkey lying on his straw lower right; the window (x 440-560, y 400-540) upper left of him with a tiny bull and plough crossing; THE END title in the upper third, clear of the donkey's face and the window.

ending.description: After the last word (176.02) THE END pops in the upper third at 176.3 and holds to 179.25. The donkey sleeps on his straw, breathing; in the window above him the tiny bull keeps ploughing across. No added moral caption.

subtitles.ar: كان تاجر يملك مزرعة فيها ثور وحمار.|كان الثور يخرج كل صباح ليحرث الأرض تحت الشمس، ثم يعود متعبًا.|أما الحمار فكان يعيش في الإسطبل، ويأكل طعامًا جيدًا ويستريح معظم الوقت.
subtitles.en: A merchant owned a farm with a bull and a donkey.|Every morning the bull went out to plow under the sun and returned exhausted.|The donkey lived in the stable, ate good food, and rested most of the time.

subtitles.ar: وفي مساء، نظر الثور إلى الحمار وقال:|«أنت محظوظ. تنام وتأكل،|أما أنا فأعمل طول النهار وأعود بجسم يؤلمني.»|شعر الحمار بالشفقة عليه، وفكر في طريقة تساعده على الراحة.
subtitles.en: One evening the bull looked at the donkey and said,|“You are lucky. You sleep and eat|while I work all day and come home aching.”|The donkey pitied him and thought of a way for him to rest.

subtitles.ar: قال الحمار: «غدًا تظاهر بأنك مريض.|إذا وضعوا المحراث عليك، استلق على الأرض ولا تقم.|وعندما يقدمون لك الطعام، لا تأكل.|سيظنون أنك لا تستطيع العمل، ويتركونك ترتاح.»
subtitles.en: The donkey said, “Tomorrow pretend to be ill.|If they put the plow on you, lie down and refuse to rise.|When they give you food, do not eat.|They will think you cannot work and let you rest.”

subtitles.ar: فعل الثور ما نصحه به الحمار.|رآه العامل مستلقيًا، ولم يستطع أن يجعله يحرث الأرض.|أخبر صاحب المزرعة أن الثور مريض.|لكن التاجر كان يفهم كلام الحيوانات، وسمع خطتهما من قبل.
subtitles.en: The bull followed the donkey’s advice.|The worker saw him lying down and could not make him plow.|He told the farmer that the bull was ill.|But the merchant understood animal speech and had already heard their plan.

subtitles.ar: قال التاجر للعامل: «اترك الثور اليوم، وخذ الحمار مكانه.»|ربط العامل المحراث بالحمار، وجعله يعمل ساعات طويلة في الحقل.|لم يكن الحمار معتادًا هذا التعب، وعاد مساءً منهكًا ومتألمًا.
subtitles.en: The merchant told the worker, “Leave the bull today and take the donkey instead.”|The worker harnessed the donkey to the plow and made him work for hours.|Unused to such labor, the donkey returned exhausted and sore that evening.

subtitles.ar: استقبل الثور الحمار بفرح وقال: «شكرًا لنصيحتك! لقد قضيت يومًا هادئًا.»|لم يرد الحمار في البداية، لأنه كان غاضبًا من نفسه.|ثم فكر كيف يخرج من هذا الموقف.
subtitles.en: The bull greeted the donkey happily and said, “Thank you for your advice! I had a peaceful day.”|At first the donkey said nothing, angry with himself.|Then he thought about how to escape this situation.

subtitles.ar: قال الحمار أخيرًا: «سمعت صاحبنا يقول إن الثور إذا بقي مريضًا غدًا،|فسيرسله إلى الجزار.»|ارتجف الثور خوفًا.|لم يعرف أن الحمار يقول هذا الكلام ليعيده إلى العمل.
subtitles.en: At last the donkey said, “I heard our owner say that if the bull remains ill tomorrow,|he will send him to the butcher.”|The bull trembled with fear.|He did not know that the donkey was saying this to get him back to work.

subtitles.ar: في الصباح التالي، نهض الثور بسرعة وأكل طعامه كله.|وعندما جاء العامل، خرج معه إلى الحقل وعاد إلى الحرث.|أما الحمار فبقي في الإسطبل يلتقط أنفاسه،|بعد أن جرب يومًا من عمل صاحبه.
subtitles.en: The next morning the bull stood up quickly and ate all his food.|When the worker came, he went out to the field and began plowing again.|The donkey stayed in the stable recovering,|having tasted a day of his companion’s work.

new_assets.name: bull
new_assets.description: Ox/bull for any farm fable. Feet at (x,y), x at body centre, facing dir. At s 1: body 260 x 150 rounded box with its top 250 above the feet; shoulder hump +30; head 110 x 100 on a short thick neck, muzzle cream; two yellow horns 70 long curving forward; nose ring r 12; legs 26 wide, 105 long; tail 120 with tuft. Pose fields: ph, amp (walk), lie 0..1 (legs fold under, body drops 95, chin to the ground at 1), headDown 0..1 (eat), headTurn -1..1 (turn the head away), neck (stretch), talk, mouth (closed, smile, frown, o, open), brow, eyes (open, wide, x, shut), ears -1..1, tongue 0..1 (lolling), snort 0..1 (nostril puffs), sag 0..1 (fatigue: head below shoulders, swayed back, bent knees), stretch 0..1, legUp (one foreleg in the air while lying), tailUp, tailDown, yoke (draw the neck yoke), yokeMark (pale rubbed band on the neck), drop, plus shared gaze, lid, wet, sq, tip.
new_assets.implementation: New file Library-style cast function bull(ctx, P) following the lion: K.rr body, ellipse hump, legs as rounded rects driven by ph/amp exactly like lion legs so walk() and footfalls() work, head group translated/rotated by headDown, headTurn and drop, eye through eye2/EYE so the acting wrapper works, red dot shading with the style's dot fill clipped to the belly half. lie blends leg length to 20 % and lowers the body; sag is a blend of drop, back curve (quadratic top edge) and knee bend. Wrap with acting(bull, () => BULLC). Draw in the story first, move to Library after approval.

Pose fields: ph, amp, lie 0..1, headDown 0..1, headTurn -1..1, neck, talk, mouth (closed, smile, smirk, frown, o, open, grit), bray 0..1 (head back, mouth wide), chew 0..1, brow, eyes (open, wide, shut), tongue, snort, sag 0..1, raise 0..1 (near foreleg lifted to point or tap), duck 0..1, tailSwish, yoke, drop, plus shared fields.

owner_questions: The merchant is shown listening at the stable window during the plan (56.7-67.1 s), before the narration reveals at 82.8-89.9 s that he had heard it; default: shown, quietly, and replayed in an inset at 87.6 s.
The butcher is shown only as a hanging shop sign with a cleaver inside the donkey's speech picture, with no blood and no butcher character; default: icon only.
The worker tries to move the bull by pulling a horn and pushing his rump, with no stick and no hitting; default: no hitting.
Invented English lettering is limited to BULL, DONKEY, PHEW!, ZZZ, FLOP!, NOPE!, AHA!, ME?!, OUCH!, GULP!, ZOOM!, CHOMP!, an HOURS counter and THE END; default: all kept.
The donkey ends with a rueful half smile and a small ear salute toward the distant bull (respect, no gloating) and no moral caption is added; default: as described.
Both time jumps to morning are handled differently: a NEXT MORNING... card at 67.2 s and a sky sweep without a card at 152.8 s (one card per film); default: one card.
implementation_notes: Start from Library/template; world width is 1600 for both sets (WW = 1600), height 1230, ground 900; clamp the camera to the 1600 width. Minimum zoom is 1.0.

Build bull and donkey first as story files on one shared quadruped base with the lion's leg code so walk(), footfalls(), kick() and dustBurst work unchanged; wrap both with acting(); set LIFE.t = t for auto-blinks and use noBlink in the held shocks (96.2-97.4, 143.9-145.9).

Every cue time is the listed word start; anticipation may lead it by up to 1.5 s as given in each action's t. Whisper word starts can include about 0.4 s of preceding silence, so check the hard accents (95.8 whip pan, 143.12 butcher sign, 155.8 spring-up) against the audio envelope.

Mirrored staging is the main device: S4 and S13 use the same two-shot and lantern with the roles swapped; S2 and S10 use the same field path, plough and worker with the animals swapped; S7 and S18 are the same doorway with opposite outcomes. Reuse the same position functions and camera keys.
Speech and thought pictures always sit in the band y 300-560 above the post, never over a face; the plan cloud moves aside at 56.7 so the window is clear for the merchant.

The merchant behind the window is the full person figure drawn behind the wall and clipped by the window hole (head and shoulders visible): place his feet at y 1010 so his face is centred in the window.
Panel-only shake for the two heaves (75.6, 76.9) and the butcher sign (143.12); the caption panel never moves.
Sound: only the nine listed effects, all in listed pauses or after the last word, SND master 0.6. No animal voice effects over narration.
Subtitles are given as verbatim chunks in subtitles[]; copy them to chunks_ar.txt and chunks_en.txt and verify by program.
Icons inside bubbles are the real cast functions at small scale, not new drawings.
warnings: Two new characters (bull, donkey) carry the whole film and neither exists in the Library; their faces must read at phone size, so test stills of the key expressions (sick act, smug, shocked, exhausted, smirk) before staging.
The side-view animals show one eye, so winks and peeks are lid pulses; make sure the 73.9 peek and the 151.9 wink read (hold at least 6 frames, add a small head turn to the lens).
S6 is 22 s in one set-up; it stays alive only if the plan cloud changes on every listed word and the merchant's entrance at 56.7 is clearly visible.
The 102.3-104.8 time-lapse has only 2.5 s for eight hours: keep it to three crossings, the sun arc and the counter.

dayCycle, thoughtCloud, painPulse, flush, inset circle, dream wash, runInPlace and the person costume presets are planned by other stories but not in the Library yet; if this film is built first it must create them under those names.
